h: The Divine Whisper Fixes Holiness Throughout the Generations

p: אֱמוֹר אֶל הַכֹּהֲנִים בְּנֵי אַהֲרֹן (וַיִּקְרָא כא, א)
"Speak to the Kohanim, the sons of Aharon" (Vayikra 21:1).
that they are the sons of Aharon?
אֶלָּא בְּנֵי אַהֲרֹן וְלֹא בְּנֵי לֵוִי
Rather: the sons of Aharon, and not the sons of Levi,
of all the Kohanim of the world, etc."
The answer needs to be understood:
that the kehunah began with Aharon
אִמְרוֹת ה׳ אֲמָרוֹת טְהוֹרוֹת (תְּהִלִּים יב, ז)
"'The sayings of Hashem are pure sayings' (Tehillim 12:7):
whatever the Holy One, blessed is He,
is for the sake of their holiness and their purity, etc."
It speaks only of the holiness of Kohanim!
וְכֵן מַה שֶּׁאָמַר אַחַר כָּךְ בְּתַנְחוּמָא
And likewise what it says afterward in the Tanchuma,
"A parable: to what is the matter comparable?
"'Speak to the Kohanim' — in a whisper, etc.;
so their saying is in a whisper, etc."
For saying refers to Torah she'b'al peh,
"My saying shall distill like the dew."
And we said that the matter is
when it comes down from heaven
is not noticed at the time it descends;
when one sees that the earth is moist,
is it noticed that dew has come down from above.
And so too Torah she'b'al peh:
in truth it is the words of the living God,
into the heart of the Sages,
as though he innovates it from his own heart;
and this is a saying in a whisper.
'And you will say in your heart'
But regarding Yisrael it is said (Yeshayahu 60:21),
"And whoever is circumcised is called a tzaddik."
is not performed by a person with his own awareness,
כִּי הוּא יֶלֶד בֶּן שְׁמוֹנָה יָמִים
for he is a child eight days old
and only the father then fulfills
nevertheless it instills holiness in him,
so that he is called a tzaddik;
and this is, from the side of Hashem Yisbarach,
And even though there are many wicked
who transgress the commandments of the Torah,
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר חֵלֶק א צג, א)
refers to milah on the eighth day.
And so with Aharon the Kohen,
who merited the holiness of the kehunah,
so that anyone who comes from his seed,
even if he does several deeds
מִכָּל מָקוֹם יֵשׁ בּוֹ קְדוּשָּׁה זוֹ
nevertheless has this holiness in him
and is forbidden to become impure to the dead.
That is why the pasuk opened
And this is the intent of Midrash Tanchuma,
which opened with the pasuk "The sayings of Hashem, etc.":
that He warns regarding the holiness of Yisrael,
for since one is circumcised he is called a tzaddik.
the Kohanim are warned regarding impurity of the dead,
even one who does not act as Aharon did.
And afterward he stated the parable,
for by right it should have been
forbidden only to the officiating Kohen,
and only through the holiness of Aharon
did he merit for all his descendants
that this holiness should be theirs.
And this is the intent of the holy Zohar:
that this is why it is written
"the sons of Aharon" and not the sons of Levi;
for Aharon, who is the beginning of all the Kohanim,
that there should be in him something of the holiness of kehunah

p: "So their saying is in a whisper:
It appears that he thereby resolves
And the matter is as stated:
saying refers to Torah she'b'al peh,
meaning that there should shine in the heart of the Kohanim
the light of Torah she'b'al peh.
"And purity is found in the Torah, etc.,
for it stands constantly in this purity
"'The fear of Hashem is pure, enduring forever':
through the fear with which Aharon feared
before the Holy One, blessed is He,
he merited that this parashah was given to him,
which does not depart from him
until the end of all generations.
And which is it? The parashah of the dead, etc."
This is as it is written (Malachi 2:5),
"And I gave them to him for fear, and he feared Me."
where it was necessary to fix the holiness
in Aharon and his sons for all eternity,
as we find in the reverse (Yoma 86b):
"Once a person has committed a transgression
it becomes to him as though permitted."
And the measure of good is greater:
it becomes fixed in their heart for all eternity,
and through this they will merit purity,
so that it will be "The fear of Hashem is pure,
did not depart from Aharon and his sons
until the end of all generations.
לֹא יִקְרְחוּ קָרְחָה וְגוֹ׳ (וַיִּקְרָא כא, ה)
"They shall not make a bald patch, etc." (Vayikra 21:5),
וְכֵן אִשָּׁה זוֹנָה וַחֲלָלָה וְגוֹ׳ (שָׁם, ז)
and likewise "A woman who is a zonah or a chalalah, etc." (Vayikra 21:7),
בְּכָל זְמַן עַד סוֹף כָּל הַדּוֹרוֹת
at all times, until the end of all generations,
"He shall not become impure to a dead person, etc." (Vayikra 21:1).
And although it is written "and say to them"
מִכָּל מָקוֹם לֹא כְּתִיב לֹא יִטַּמְּאוּ
nevertheless it does not write "they shall not become impure,"
as the holy Zohar also asks
they merited to have fixed in each one,
in the language of the singular;
in the language of the many.
the Holy One, blessed is He,
with one heart and one will
when they stood at Mount Sinai, etc."
That is: at the assembly at Mount Sinai
and it is stated (in the Mechilta, Bachodesh 1):
that it was said to them in the singular,
and then it was fixed for all eternity:
Torah study was implanted in their heart,
and at the utterance "You shall have no,"
the yetzer hara was uprooted from their heart
(as they said in Shir HaShirim Rabbah
on the pasuk "Let him kiss me," 1:2).
This is not so in parashas Kedoshim,
which is written in the plural
And so too the difference here:
that the parashah of impurity of the dead
for there was fixed in them for all eternity,
until the end of all generations,
שֶׁהוּא יִרְאַת ה׳ טְהוֹרָה עוֹמֶדֶת לָעַד
that is "The fear of Hashem is pure, enduring forever":
that stands constantly in this purity
This is not so with the parashah of
"They shall not make a bald patch, etc.,"
וְכֵן אִשָּׁה זוֹנָה וַחֲלָלָה וְגוֹ׳ לֹא יִקָּחוּ
and likewise "A woman who is a zonah or a chalalah, etc., they shall not take"
this is written in the plural,
for in this they did not merit such a level
that it be stated in the singular;
רַק כְּתִיב קְדוֹשִׁים יִהְיוּ וְגוֹ׳ (שָׁם, ו)
only "They shall be holy, etc." is written (Vayikra 21:6).
אַךְ מִכָּל מָקוֹם כְּתִיב אַחַר כָּךְ
Yet nevertheless it is written afterward,
at the end, also in the singular,
"For he is holy to his God,
and you shall sanctify him, etc." (Vayikra 21:7–8):
for in the end they will merit this too,
that it be in the singular
and be fixed for all generations.
this Moshe Rabbeinu caused to shine in them,
so that it was said to them in the singular:
that each one of the Kohanim,
whoever is of the sons of Aharon,
merits to have the purity fixed in him
And this came about through the saying
which is a saying in secret,
And this is what is meant in the holy Zohar
דְּבֵיהּ אִתְרְעֵי קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא מִכּוּלָּא
for in him the Holy One, blessed is He, took pleasure above all,
in order to make peace, etc."
"For the lips of a Kohen, etc.,
and Torah they shall seek from his mouth";
וְכֵן וְהוּא יִהְיֶה לְּךָ לְפֶה (שְׁמוֹת ד, טז)
and likewise, "And he shall be a mouth for you" (Shemos 4:16).
is the one who joins heaven and earth
"who holds on to heaven and to earth"
the Written Torah and Torah she'b'al peh,
and through him comes the drawing down
from the Written Torah to Torah she'b'al peh;
so too Aharon, whose attribute is peace, etc.,
the sons of Aharon, the Kohanim,
that the purity should endure forever.

inlineHeadings.text: Repeated Saying Fixes Purity in the Heart
Each Kohen Receives an Enduring Personal Holiness
